name: Elasticsearch
description: Protects against destructive Elasticsearch REST API operations like index deletion, \ delete-by-query, index close, and cluster setting changes.

destructive_patterns.name: es-curl-delete-doc
destructive_patterns.description: curl -X DELETE against /_doc deletes a document from Elasticsearch.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a document removes it from the index. The document ID becomes \ available for reuse. Applications expecting this document will receive \ 404 errors. Search results will no longer include this document.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET the document first to verify \ - Use document versioning for conflict detection \ - Index a tombstone document instead of deleting

destructive_patterns.name: es-curl-delete-by-query
destructive_patterns.description: curl -X POST to _delete_by_query deletes documents matching the query.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Delete-by-query removes all documents matching the query criteria. A \ malformed query can delete far more documents than intended. The operation \ runs asynchronously and cannot be easily cancelled once started.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Run the query with _search first to preview matches \ - Use scroll_size to limit batch size \ - Set wait_for_completion=false and monitor progress

destructive_patterns.name: es-curl-close-index
destructive_patterns.description: curl -X POST to _close closes an index, making it unavailable for reads/writes.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Closing an index blocks all read and write operations. Applications will \ receive errors when accessing closed indices. Closed indices still consume \ disk space but release memory. Use _all with extreme caution.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET /_cat/indices to review indices first \ - Close specific indices rather than patterns \ - Use index lifecycle management for automated handling

destructive_patterns.name: es-curl-delete-index
destructive_patterns.description: curl -X DELETE against an Elasticsearch index (or _all/*) deletes data permanently.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an index permanently removes all documents, mappings, and settings. \ Using _all or * wildcards can delete multiple indices at once. This operation \ is immediate and irreversible. Data cannot be recovered without snapshots.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET /_cat/indices to review before deletion \ - Create a snapshot before deleting \ - Disable action.destructive_requires_name for safety

destructive_patterns.name: es-curl-cluster-settings
destructive_patterns.description: curl -X PUT to /_cluster/settings changes cluster settings and can be dangerous.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Cluster settings affect all nodes and can impact stability, performance, \ and data integrity. Persistent settings survive restarts. Changes to \ allocation, recovery, or shard settings can trigger data movement.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET /_cluster/settings to review current values \ - Use transient settings for testing \ - Test changes on non-production clusters first
